proof: For a built generation with a known bound, every accepted finite expiry is nonnegative and the bound is no greater than each such original expiry. Zero expiry retains the existing immortal normalization; any accepted negative expiry makes the bound unknown permanently for that generation.

If0<=now<bound<=expiry<=i64::MAX, mathematical now-expiry is negative and representable in i64, so wrapping_sub equals ordinary subtraction. Disabled andSeconds0 live predicates succeed; positive stale intervals also succeed. Forever is live for every expiry and clock. Negative now, unknown bound and now>=bound use the original path.

Only accepted records update the bound: static-suppressed records return before entry or parent creation. All actual forward entries and reverse owners are among accepted records. Every synthetic nonterminal is derived from an accepted record. Parent extension only takes max or becomes immortal, never shortens a finite expiry.

Name and reverse expiry only deactivate entries or remove nonterminals. Leaving the old bound early cannot skip a necessary removal. Inactive entries stay inactive after rollback. Derived Clone copies the bound with the data; Arc copy-on-write preserves the same state. Rebuild calls build with retained inputs and current hosts, recalculating the bound for the new published view.

LeasePolicy is private immutable generation state; policy() returns a copy. No external field setter can change expiry, active entries, parent data or policy without the reviewed construction/mutation paths.
